references.text: Abraham received sheep, cattle, and servants in Egypt, which mirrors Isaac's wealth with flocks, herds, and many servants.
Abraham was very rich in livestock, silver, and gold, reflecting Isaac's material blessings in Gerar.
The Philistines' jealousy toward Isaac led Abimelek to ask him to move away, a direct consequence of the wealth described in verse 14.
Jacob became extremely wealthy with large amounts of flocks, female servants, male servants, camels, and donkeys—a continuation of God's blessings through the patriarchs.
Joseph's brothers were jealous of him, paralleling the Philistines' jealousy toward Isaac due to his wealth.
Job was the greatest of all the men of the East, with large herds and a great household, reminiscent of Isaac's wealth and blessing.
The psalm emphasizes that wealth and abundance are found in the house of the righteous, reflecting God's blessings upon Isaac.
Thematic parallel: God's blessing brings abundance of livestock and riches to His servant.
Direct narrative connection: Description of the infrastructure for the blessed wealth.
